lines.text: I'm Lakshmi. My husband Raghu and I run a hardware shop in Coimbatore. Every Friday, we pay our suppliers.
The bills come in Tamil, Hindi and English, some written by hand. Last month, one bill had a new bank account on it. It wasn't our supplier's.
So now we use Nipta. Let me show you a Friday.
I sign in and add this week's bills. Nipta reads each one, and checks it six ways before any money moves.
Then it gives me one list for today. What to pay, what to check, and what it won't pay.
Tamil Tools wrote four thousand five hundred. But the items only add up to four thousand three hundred. Nipta stops it, and shows me both numbers.
This is the old trick. Eastern Hardware printed a new bank account on the bill. Nipta only pays the account I saved myself, and there is no button to pay it anyway.
Kaveri Fasteners sent the same bill twice, with a new number and date. Nipta matches the items, and puts it aside for me.
I can ask in Kannada, Hindi or English. Which bills are fine? It answers in my language. And asking never pays anything.
Coimbatore Packing is clean, and due first. I open the payment. It shows the exact amount, and my saved account.
I approve three thousand two hundred rupees. Only then can it go out through Cashfree. Today is a practice run, so no real money moves. Press twice, it still pays once, and it shows the real status.
Every step is written down. Which bill, which check, who approved it, and what the bank said.
The right bill, to the right person, for the right amount. That's Nipta.
